findings.description: The policy grants ec2:*, s3:*, lambda:*, and cloudwatch:* on Resource "*" to the svc_deploy user, giving it full control of compute, storage, serverless, and logging services, including reading every S3 object in the account, terminating or launching EC2 instances, and deleting CloudWatch logs to cover tracks. This wildcard-action/wildcard-resource grant with no least-privilege scoping violates least privilege and can lead to full account compromise if the accompanying access key leaks.

A static IAM access key pair is created for the svc_deploy user, which holds a wildcard administrative policy. Unlike short-lived role credentials or OIDC federation, these keys never rotate automatically, do not expire, and persist until manually deleted, so leaked material grants persistent, unexpiring high-privilege access.

aws_iam_access_key stores the secret access key in Terraform state, and the output "svc_deploy_key_material" surfaces the encrypted_secret value. Anyone with read access to state, plan files, CI logs, or output consumers can recover reusable credentials for the fully privileged svc_deploy user.
